_comment: Known gaps shown by jarvis-status. Edited here, not in the script, so closing a gap is a data change rather than a code change. A gap NEVER makes the overall status FAIL -- it is a documented limitation, not a fault.

gaps.note: Settled by measurement 2026-09-09 -- see jarvis-wake-benchmark/docs/WAKE_WORD_RESOLUTION.md. Cause is the English acoustic model vs Japanese pronunciation, and neither threshold tuning nor an engine swap closes it. Capture path is exonerated (played TTS through the jack mic scored 0.9990 FIRE; ambient clipped 0 samples). Engine is exonerated (English TTS 0.9470). Sweeping openWakeWord over sensitivity 0.10-0.40 x confirmation_frames 1-4 found NO combination with recall>=90% and FP<=0.5/h: current (frames=1, thr=0.35) gives recall 23.3%, and the best case (frames=1, thr=0.10) only 60.0%. Japanese TTS scores median 0.1274 against the 0.35 threshold -- about one third -- so utterance-to-utterance variation straddles the boundary, which is why it 'sometimes' works. confirmation_frames: 1 is not a disabled safeguard but a necessity: frames=2 drops recall to 3.3%. sherpa KWS was fetched and measured too (its deps pypinyin/sentencepiece were missing, so it had never run in production): open-vocab accepts romanised keywords ('HEI JAABISU' tokenises) but Japanese recall is 0.0-4.8% because gigaspeech is an English acoustic model. DECISION: keep sensitivity 0.35 / confirmation_frames 1 unchanged, use Cmd+Shift+J as the daily path (measured 7.9s end to end, Physical Hotkey 10/10 PASS), and say 'Hey Jarvis' English-style when voice wake is wanted. FUTURE (user intent 2026-09-09): a Japanese custom model is the only remaining route, and it is also the only way to wake on a nickname -- hey_jarvis is a fixed model so the phrase cannot be chosen. Training needs a GPU; the user has Linux + RTX 5070 Ti. harness/sweep.py and harness/wake_probe.py built today are reusable for validating any such model.

Recovery from a clamshell sleep/wake cycle has still never been observed -- and 2026-09-09 measurement shows why: this machine does not sleep. `pmset -g custom` reports `sleep 0` for AC Power (and `displaysleep 0`), Amphetamine held PreventUserIdleSystemSleep for 21h40m, and `pmset -g log` reported `Total Sleep/Wakes since boot at 2026-09-08 19:38:41 +0900 :0` -- zero cycles since the reboot that started this runtime. The user works clamshell on AC through a DisplayLink dock, so idle sleep never fires. This gap was previously ranked low as 'never observed'; it was then briefly ranked HIGH on the assumption that clamshell operation exercises it, which was wrong -- clamshell operation on AC actively prevents it. Re-ranked LOW. It becomes reachable only if the machine runs on battery and sleeps, or if the power configuration changes. jarvis-status surfaces this precondition in the Power row so the next attempt does not re-derive it.
